title: Uniform fragment credits and call-consistency fix for SSE streaming
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Streaming clients intermittently observed truncated or interleaved JSON objects when an SSE connection experienced mid-stream partial frames. In production this produced occasional: 1) malformed partial JSON events, 2) function/tool call ordering inversion when a tool sentinel crossed a fragment boundary, and 3) duplicate delimiters emitted during retryed reassembly. Reproduction: fuzzer harness (added) reproduces the mid-frame split at varying byte offsets and with interleaved heartbeats. Motivation: existing heuristic for allowing byte "credits" per fragment drifted when fragments were coalesced or split by proxies/NGINX, which led to delimiter shifts and incorrectly acknowledged function-call handoffs. Fix summary: 1) Introduce a uniform fragment-credit accounting model (byte-window + sequence slot) so each fragment carries an explicit credit token that survives coalescing/splitting. 2) Implement a deterministic call-handshake state machine: function/tool-call sentinels now require a two-step ACK/lease handshake before the consumer will reorder or emit the call boundary. 3) Canonicalize trailing delimiter emission: the streamer normalizes delimiter sequences into a single canonical boundary and defers emission until the credit token is validated. 4) Tighten UTF-8 escape handling at fragment edges to avoid partial-escape misclassification. 5) Add targeted unit and integration tests plus a randomized fuzz target (sse_fragment_fuzz_test) to cover split/coalesce/heartbeat combos. Checklist: - [x] Add uniform fragment-credit token and accounting across sse/parser and sse/streamer - [x] Add deterministic call-handshake logic and lease window - [x] Canonicalize delimiter emission path and add tests for duplicate/remove cases - [x] Add fuzz test harness and CI job (non-blocking on faster lanes) - [x] Update openai_compat adapter to propagate fragment-credit header - [x] Add changelog entry and release note blurb Rationale notes: This approach favors determinism over opportunistic merging of fragments. It slightly increases per-fragment metadata (a 1-2 byte token) but prevents pernicious ordering bugs that previously required ad-hoc fixes. Related: Linear ENG-4821 tracks customer-observed malformed JSON incidents; SUP-1324 is the support escalation from a customer reproducer. Links: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821, https://jira.redwood.internal/browse/SUP-1324

review_conversation: Liam Rodriguez (review): The overall design looks sound; two questions: 1) do two-step ACKs add latency for fast-path small messages? 2) how will this interact with existing prefix caching?

Maya Chen (author): ACKs are lease-based and default to a zero-round-trip fast-path when fragments are single-shot (no split). The code paths are guarded so prefix caching — which uses immutable KV caches — only sees credits during reassembly windows.

Priya Kapoor (review): Please add a unit test for a 1-byte split inside a UTF-8 4-byte sequence — previous incidents came from that exact case. Also mark the fuzz CI job non-blocking on the quick lane.
Maya Chen (author): Added utf8 boundary tests and adjusted CI tagging; fuzz job added to nightly and non-blocking in PR lanes.
Evan Morales (approval): Verified with local canary against a replay log from SUP-1324; ordering now preserved and handoffs deterministic. Approving.

ci_summary: CI build: passed; unit tests: all green; integration: 2 flaky tests rerun and passed; fuzz job added to nightly; lint: fixed warnings on re-run
release_notes: Fix streaming: prevents partial-JSON corruption and function/tool-call reordering by introducing a fragment-credit token and deterministic call-handshake. Added fuzz coverage and updated openai_compat adapter to maintain compatibility.
notes_for_ops: Canary rollout recommended (5% traffic for 24h) to validate in the wild; watch sse.malformed_json.rate and sse.toolcall.reorder.count for regressions. If issues appear, fallback via routing policy to previous stream adapter (openai_compat vX) is supported.
qa_steps: 1) Run tests/sse/sse_fragment_fuzz_test.go locally; 2) Start streamer with --enable-fragment-credits and pipe a recorded SUP-1324 replay; 3) Validate no partial JSON errors and stable toolcall ordering; 4) Monitor metrics listed in notes_for_ops

estimated_risks: Low-medium: adds small per-fragment metadata and a new handshake path; risk mitigated by canary and ability to route to legacy adapter.
